cim: 1Password launches secure sign-in platform for artificial intelligence agents
cim_eredeti: 1Password launches secure sign-in platform for artificial intelligence agents
szoveg_eredeti:
1Password has introduced a new sign-in platform designed specifically for personal artificial intelligence agents to access user accounts securely without exposing passwords, based on information published by Silicon Angle.

The platform addresses security risks associated with users pasting credentials directly into AI chat windows, a practice that often leaves sensitive data vulnerable. By utilizing a unique digital key, the system allows agents from companies such as Meta Platforms Inc., Anthropic PBC, OpenAI Group PBC, and SpaceXSI to authenticate requests without ever accessing the actual password.

Instead, the service requires human approval on a personal device before automatically filling in credentials. This approach ensures that agents only receive temporary, task-specific access rather than permanent account control. Major industry players, including OpenAI and Anthropic, have already begun integrating this technology into their respective AI assistants. Additionally, nine other companies are currently developing similar integrations to enhance security for their users.

This development aligns with broader industry efforts to establish task-based access protocols for autonomous systems, ensuring that AI agents maintain appropriate permission levels while performing work on behalf of users. The company serves over 200,000 businesses, including major entities like Canva Pty Ltd. and Stripe Inc., though specific rollout timelines for these new integrations remain unannounced.
